name: og-05-environmental-to-internal-bioenergetics
title: Environmental to internal bioenergetics (Campaign V)
question: Can selection move from externally imposed gradients toward internally maintained electrochemical states (catalytic ion transport then pumping)?
hypothesis: When membrane permeability, Na+/H+ coupling and catalyst efficiency vary under selection, systems with increasing internal gradient generation win on throughput + persistence — but only if membranes stay sufficiently leaky (Sojo constraint).
objective: Allow catalytic ion transport and active pumping; test whether selection favors internalized gradient generation.
proposed_models_methods: evolutionary control loop over membrane parameters

conditions.name: reproducibility
conditions.expr: solver and db and seed and scenario recorded

contract.note: bigraph-schema typed ports (_type/_units/bounds) + conservation predicates; the composite built for this study must declare a ProcessContract matching this face (audited via the workbench §Contract panel).

behavior_tests.name: selection-internalizes-gradient-generation
behavior_tests.description: As the external gradient declines, selection drives the population to internalize gradient generation (active-pump fraction rises past 0.6).

measure.detail: active-pump fraction of the surviving population at the collapsed gradient

pass_if.detail: the population internalizes (pump fraction >= 0.6) as the external gradient falls

behavior_tests.name: reduced-gradient-dependence
behavior_tests.description: An internalizing (efficient-pump) lineage persists as the external gradient is lowered (survivors stay high).

measure.detail: surviving strategy mass at the collapsed external gradient

pass_if.detail: internalizing lineage persists (survivors >= 0.5) at the collapsed gradient

behavior_tests.name: sojo-constraint-weak-pump-collapses
behavior_tests.description: Discriminating (Sojo 2014): a weak pump cannot internalize, so when the external gradient collapses the lineage goes extinct — only sufficiently efficient pumps survive the transition.

pass_if.detail: the weak-pump control collapses (survivors ~0) where the efficient pump persists

behavior_tests.name: energy-cost-accounted
behavior_tests.description: Membrane-maintenance energy is outweighed by benefit in the surviving population (net-positive free-energy flux).

literature_anchors.expectation: LUCA-like cells can use proton gradients only if membranes remain sufficiently leaky
literature_anchors.status_in_workspace: Not yet measurable — module processes not built

claim: Under a declining external gradient, selection drives an efficient-pump population to internalize gradient generation (pump fraction 0→0.95) and persist, while a weak-pump lineage collapses — the Sojo-2014 leaky-membrane constraint on bioenergetic internalization.
result: Efficient pump internalizes (final 0.95) and survives (survivors 1.0); the weak-pump control collapses (survivors 0) as the gradient falls.

findings.statement: As the external geochemical gradient declines over the run, replicator selection drives the population from externally-driven (pump fraction ~0) to internalized gradient generation (pump fraction ~0.95) while persisting — the bioenergetic internalization is an evolutionary outcome, not a scripted upgrade.

evidence.observed: internalization 0.00 -> 0.95; survivors 1.0 at the collapsed gradient

findings.explanation: BioenergeticSelectionProcess replicator dynamics over a (permeability × pump) strategy grid with a Sojo leaky-membrane fitness; the declining gradient flips the winning strategy from leaky-external to tight-pump.

findings.statement: A weak pump cannot internalize — when the external gradient collapses, the weak-pump lineage goes extinct (survivors → 0) while the efficient-pump lineage persists. Internalization is only viable with a sufficiently efficient pump (the Sojo leaky-membrane constraint).

evidence.observed: efficient survivors 1.0 vs weak-pump survivors 0.0 at collapsed gradient

findings.explanation: Below a pump-efficiency threshold the internal-pump flux cannot beat its cost against the lost external coupling, so no strategy clears the survival floor.

report.title: Campaign V — environmental to internal bioenergetics
report.verdict: PASS — selection internalizes gradient generation; the Sojo constraint bounds it
report.main_insight: Under a declining external gradient, selection favors internalized gradient generation — but only where the pump is efficient enough (the Sojo leaky-membrane constraint); a weak pump goes extinct at the transition.
report.conclusion: The evolutionary control loop shows the final pre-LUCA transition: lineages move from externally imposed to internally maintained electrochemical states under selection, bounded by the Sojo requirement. Closes the pre-genetic milestone of the campaign.
report.caveat: Coarse-grained deterministic replicator dynamics (the proposed primary method), not a wrapped ALife/MD engine. The fitness is a Sojo-grounded reduced model with calibrated couplings.

biological_validation.basis: Reproduces the Sojo-2014 constraint — internalization is viable only with a sufficiently efficient pump; a weak pump collapses at the transition.

explanatory_gain.basis: The evolutionary control loop explains both the internalization transition and its Sojo-bounded failure mode from the leaky-membrane fitness.

limitations: Coarse-grained deterministic replicator dynamics with calibrated couplings; not a wrapped ALife/MD engine.
Single declining-gradient scenario; the pump-efficiency threshold is shown by two arms, not a full sweep.

resolved_uncertainties: Selection can internalize gradient generation as the external gradient falls, bounded by the Sojo leaky-membrane constraint.
remaining_uncertainties: The precise pump-efficiency threshold separating viable internalization from extinction.

followup_study_proposals.rationale: Sweep catalyst_efficiency and decline_rate to map the viable-internalization boundary.

expert_questions: Reward throughput, persistence, or a weighted combination for the selection objective?
